intended_object: The standard isomorphism SL_n(R) ≅ Hom_{K-alg}(K[SL_n], R) for any commutative ring K and commutative K-algebra R. Here K[SL_n] = K[GL_n]/(det − 1), and the Hom-set is a group under convolution, the group law coming from the Hopf-algebra structure. This identifies the R-points of the special linear group scheme with SL_n(R). I took this from the docstring, the module documentation, and how the library uses it later (specialLinearGroupMulEquivPoints, specialLinearGroupPointsIso).
explanation:
The coordinate ring is built correctly. It is the localization of K[x_ij] at det (this is K[GL_n]), divided by the ideal generated by det(X) − 1.

The forward map sends s ∈ SL_n(R) to its evaluation map. This map is well defined on the quotient because det s = 1. The inverse map reads off the matrix of images of the universal entries, and its determinant is 1 because det(X) = 1 holds in the quotient. Both inverse laws are proved.

The multiplicative structure on the Hom side is Mathlib's convolution product (WithConv), which is the group law on the points of an affine group scheme. Multiplicativity comes from the corresponding statement for GL, using the fact that the quotient map is a bialgebra map.

The generality is the natural one: an arbitrary commutative base ring K, an arbitrary finite index type n with decidable equality, and an arbitrary commutative K-algebra R. Placing n in the same universe as K is harmless. I found no special linear (or general linear) group scheme in Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry directory, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
